summary.headline: RIR Power Electronics FY26 revenue rose 5.41% to INR90.87 crores and PAT reached INR6.72 crores, while Q4 revenue fell 9.5% YoY on a one-time order base.
summary.overview: Standalone Q4 FY26 revenue from operations was INR23.95 crores, up 18.16% QoQ but down 9.5% YoY against a one-time INR3.3 crore order executed in March 2025; Q4 EBITDA was INR2.09 crores and PAT INR1.39 crores. For FY26, revenue was INR90.87 crores, EBITDA INR10.21 crores, PAT INR6.72 crores and EPS INR0.86, with order intake of INR90.2 crores and closing backlog of INR17.4 crores. The main open issue is the 33 kV power connection for the Odisha plant, which has slipped from March to a committed June-end/July target, delaying epitaxy start to Q2 FY27. Management also announced its first overseas order (5kV press-pack SCRs) and a 25kV, 120kA capacitor discharge switch development.

financial_highlights.change: +18.16% QoQ; -9.5% YoY (YoY base inflated by one-time INR3.3 crore order in March 2025)

segments.name: Halol (Gujarat) facility
segments.commentary: Current manufacturing base; single shift operation at present. Management targets 2x to 3x turnover in 2 to 3 years via productivity gains and about INR5 crore accrual-funded upgrades to furnaces and testing facilities.

segments.name: Odisha facility (epitaxy, packaging, fabrication)
segments.commentary: Phase 1 (epitaxy and packaging) clean room complete for epitaxy; plant and machinery installation under way. Epi wafers to be sold to overseas fabricators and SiC devices outsourced for validation, with revenue targeted in FY27.

segments.name: Defence and railways
segments.commentary: Army high-power module developed and accepted after testing, with multiple orders expected over five years. Railways remain a major client; new railway product specifications are being developed.

guidance_outlook: Odisha 33 kV power supply committed by State government for end-June; plant and machinery installation expected complete by July end.
Epitaxy operations expected to commence in Q2 FY27 (August-September 2026), per management.
Odisha revenue expected from FY27 via Epi wafer sales and outsourced SiC device validation.

Total Odisha project capex about INR618 crores; about INR120 crores spent so far (50% State subsidy); remaining about INR500 crores (INR100 crores Phase 1, INR400 crores Phase 2) with 50% subsidy expected; full capex by December 2027 or March 2028.
Halol turnover target of 2x to 3x in 2 to 3 years, with power-sector growth expected to take longer for approvals.
Management expects the 5kV SCR order (120 press-pack devices, 125 mm) to be completed by end-2026 in phases.
capex_capacity: Odisha capex: about INR120 crores spent, INR500 crores yet to be undertaken; asset turnover expected around 0.65x, versus a global industry range of 0.5x to 0.75x.
About INR5 crores from internal accruals to upgrade Halol facility and testing for defence and the 125 mm 5kV thyristor.
Bank term loan of about INR100 crores for Odisha packaging facility: in-principle approval received, conditions being fulfilled before sanction.
Halol operates one shift; management says two or three shifts are feasible if required.
Breakeven for Odisha fab estimated at about 60-65% capacity utilisation; margins above 40% thereafter (management view).
demand_pricing: First overseas order: supply of 120 units of 125 mm, 5kV press-pack SCR thyristors for high-voltage DC transmission; phased execution, completion by end-2026.
Management cites planned Government of India HVDC transmission of about 2,500 MW over five to seven years, with no domestic valve supplier currently.
Management expects 20-25% share in medium and high power segments; low power to be served with value-added offerings to compete with Chinese supply.
Exports seen rising faster than domestic demand over the last three to four months; management says import and export volumes are currently broadly matched, limiting rupee-depreciation benefit.
Contract manufacturing JV continues for 1200 V and 1700 V; a Korean source being evaluated for 3.3 kV.

qa_highlights.question: What are the Odisha capex plan, subsidy and milestone terms, and asset turnover?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said total capex is about INR618 crores, with about INR120 crores spent and 50% subsidy from Odisha government; asset turnover expected around 0.65x, versus a global range of 0.5x to 0.75x. Full capex expected by December 2027 or March 2028. Milestone clawback terms were not addressed.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 33 kV power connection for Odisha on track, and is the production timeline still valid?
qa_highlights.answer: Not yet received. State government has committed to end-June; a transformer is being hired and line work is in parallel with erection, targeted for mid to end July. Management says epitaxy will start in Q2 FY27 (August-September). Harshad Mehta said DG sets were considered but not viable.

qa_highlights.question: Has bank financing been finalised?
qa_highlights.answer: The about INR100 crore bank loan is for packaging, not working capital. In-principle approval is in place with some conditions being fulfilled before sanction.

qa_highlights.question: Any repeat orders from Navy or Army, and what about one-time orders?
qa_highlights.answer: Management acknowledged the orders are one-time but described them as the start of follow-on work: Army module accepted with multiple orders expected over five years; Navy SiC devices are under vendor testing.

qa_highlights.question: Will strategic investors or domestic institutions be inducted?
qa_highlights.answer: Ankit Shah said talks with strategic partners are ongoing and will be disclosed once firmed up; current holders are FPIs and FIIs plus some sub-1% institutions.

qa_highlights.question: What is the NSE listing status?
qa_highlights.answer: Clarifications have been responded to; approval awaited in due course.

qa_highlights.question: What are the Halol expansion limits and product plans?
qa_highlights.answer: Halol expected to reach 2.5x to 3x with productivity gains and modest equipment upgrades; beyond 3x, capacity constraint likely, with possible shifting of products to Odisha. Railway and defence product upgrades are cannibalising some existing products but adding value; power sector and EV/inverter OEMs are being targeted.

risks_watch: Odisha power connection (33 kV) has slipped from March to end-June/July; further delay pushes epitaxy start beyond Q2 FY27 and makes a DG-set fallback costly.
Odisha project depends on State government and grid agencies; Tata Power as service provider awaiting transformers.
Q4 YoY revenue decline; FY26 growth of 5.41% is modest and order book (INR17.4 crores) is small relative to FY26 intake of INR90.2 crores.
Bank term loan (about INR100 crores) and strategic investor deal not yet finalised.
Commoditisation risk in low-power products and Chinese competition, per analyst questions; management response was qualitative.
Rupee depreciation benefit limited as imports and exports are broadly matched, per management.
summary.management_tone: Confident and forward-looking on strategy and long-term demand, but noticeably defensive and vague on the Odisha power delay, where timelines have slipped repeatedly. Several answers on capital allocation, strategic investors and the contract manufacturing JV were deflected or left without specifics.
key_quotes: Power electronics is a bridge that will enable the power which is right now generated with 70s technology will enable that power to be adequately supplied to the loads that require the reliability and performance.
Unfortunately, this is even though we manage power, we don't produce power or we don't transmit or distribute power.
Till you get to that breakeven at about 60 % or 65% fab capacity, you don't make any money, as a matter of fact you need to get there to breakeven.
